itemUsage.en: Armed escort and jianghu wanderer Windscoot rarely ever draws the twin blades at his waist, not unless strictly necessary.
itemUsage.zh: 行走江湖的镖客骋风，腰间的双刀轻易不拔出来——除非逼不得已。

itemDesc.en: Most of the time, he prefers to talk things out. But he's discovered this goes a lot easier when you have swords on your belt.
itemDesc.zh: 大部分时候，他喜欢以理服人。但他发现，这一招似乎在佩刀的时候才比较好使。

description.en:
Operator Windscoot has demonstrated excellent timing when dealing with perilous combat situations.
The Field Operations Department has thus passed the following resolution:
This operator shall be appointed a Guard Operator during field operations to exercise Liberator responsibilities.
In witness whereof,
This badge is hereby conferred upon the above named.

特别颁发此证章

description.en:
After a huge ruckus, the two elders from Gang of Justice reluctantly depart, leaving the place in a mess—wooden chairs smashed over heads, shattered windows broken with bodies, and their iconic wooden sign on the door with 'Yi', or 'justice', written on it, now split into two pieces stuck in the ground.
'Anyone who was injured should head inside to get patched up. Everyone else help me clean up the mess. If any of our customers see this, they're going to be scared away.' Windscoot says this as he takes the lead and grabs a broom with one hand, his other pressing on a cut on his forearm.
'Hey, kid. You're the one who should go get patched up. If you hadn't blocked that blow for me, my head would've been split open.'
'It's just a little cut, I'm not afraid of blood—okay, okay! Enough glaring at me, uncle. I'll go wrap it up once I'm done cleaning.'
The former bandits begin to clumsily clean up the mess. Today their 'escort agency' has far less members than when they were bandits, and the situation seems much more somber after this bout of chaos. Someone picks up the broken 'Yi' and says: 'Are we gonna toss our Justice away just like that?'
Windscoot takes the broken sign and sighs without speaking. The Gang of Justice had broken up, and the escort agency's business was unlikely to improve. Was everything he had done so far the right thing to do?
'Hey,' The uncle jabs at him, 'You did nothing wrong. It was those two who extorted our customers. If they'd carried on with it, it would've been hard for us to continue this line of work.'
'Exactly! I finally learned to read a few words recently too. Wouldn't it all go to waste if our agency goes bankrupt?!'
'And all those super-hard-to-remember passcodes too!'
'Don't get me even started. Those damn traffic rules keep giving me fines round the clock! I won't forgive anyone who makes all my effort go to waste!'
'Haha, isn't that because you're too dumb?'
The crowd chats about the efforts they've put into their new lives, filling the air with laughs. Windscoot unfurrows his brow, and pats his own head, as if trying to expel the hesitation within himself.
The next day, the wooden 'Yi' sign appears again at the escort agency's entrance.
'For now, I just stuck them back together with some nails. I'll make a new one when I have time.' Windscoot returns to his usual cheerful tone.
'Nah, don't bother! This is a pretty unique look. Look at the top and bottom halves—now they're joined even closer than before!'
'Exactly, isn't it the trend these days to have, uh, a logo or whatever? We should trademark it!' Sounds of agreement follow.
'Really? I'll go find someone to turn it into an actual logo then, and print it on our clothes and gear. But remember: you asked for this, so no refusing to wear your future uniforms.'
Windscoot's beaming smile draws a crowd of complaints. Learning to write up orders, practicing martial arts, keeping proper accounts—everyone is busy getting the escort agency on the right track.
description.zh:
大闹一场之后，那两位义帮元老不甘心地离开了，留下满地狼藉——被脑袋砸坏的木椅，被身体撞碎的窗户，还有那块原本竖在门口的、标志性的“义”字木牌，从中间断成两截，陷在了土里。
“受伤的人去屋里包扎，其他的叔叔阿姨，跟我一起把地面打扫干净吧。万一客人看到这幅景象会被吓跑的。”骋风一边说着，一边率先抓起扫帚，另一只手压着小臂上汩汩流血的伤口。
“喂，小子，你才最该包扎。要不是你帮我挡了那一下，我就该脑袋开花了。”
“就是点小擦伤，我没那么娇气……好好好，小叔，别瞪我，我干完活就去包扎。”
昔日的匪徒们笨手笨脚地开始打扫。如今的“镖局”，人数比做山贼时少了一大半，在一片凌乱中更显凄清。有人拾起那断成两半的“义”字：“我们的义，就要这样丢掉了吗？”
骋风接过那断掉的木牌，叹气不语。义帮已经分裂，镖局生意也不见得会有起色，他至今为止的努力，真的都是对的吗？
“喂，”小叔给了他一拳，“你没做错。是那两个家伙勒索客人有错在先。被他们这么搞下去，以后我们生意都难做。”
“就是啊，我才刚认得几个字，万一镖局黄了，不白学了？！”
“还有那些难记得要死的暗号！”
“别提了，那该死的交通规则害我成天挨罚！谁要让我白记那么一通，我可饶不了他！”
“哈哈，还不是因为你脑袋太笨！”
众人聊起为新生活付出的汗水，镖局里一时充满了欢声笑语。骋风释然地松开了眉头，拍拍脑袋，仿佛要赶走内心的迟疑。
第二天，镖局门口的义字木牌竟重新出现。
“我临时用钉子钉了一下，等有空了就做块新的。”骋风恢复了爽朗的语调。
“不用！我看这样挺别致。你看这‘义’字的上下两半，连得比之前还紧哩！”
“就是，现在不都流行——那叫什么，商标吗？我看啊，这就当做我们镖局的商标好了！”这话引来了一片赞同声。
“真的？那我就去找人把它设计成商标，印在我们的衣服和工具上。所以，叔叔阿姨们，既然是你们自己要求的——以后制服可不许不穿了。”
骋风笑眯眯地说出的话引来了一大片抱怨。学打单子、练武、记账，众人正为镖局走上正轨而忙碌着。
